overview: Mercurial Swift is a bounty hunter from Coruscant, documented across Comics · War of the Bounty Hunters. Core world hunter competing in War of the Bounty Hunters after Han Solo carbonite theft.
history:
Mercurial Swift rose from Coruscant to become a bounty hunter whose name appears on guild boards from the Core to the Outer Rim. Mercurial Swift built Coruscant Core-world hunter reputation for speed and agility before joining the chaotic competition for Han Solo's stolen carbonite block in War of the Bounty Hunters. Bounty puck archives, Imperial warrant logs, and Hutt contract registries all document Mercurial Swift as a contractor who shaped wars without wearing a uniform. Coverage spans all nine saga films, Clone Wars, Rebels, Mandalorian, Book of Boba Fett, Andor, KOTOR, KOTOR II, SWTOR, and Sith Empire-era mercenary markets.

Even before Mercurial Swift's career, Coruscant produced hunters, soldiers, and syndicate enforcers whose traditions fed the modern guild system. Coruscant guild posting boards historically favored Core-trained hunters with political connections; Swift represents urban hunter elite in post-Endor comics crossover. Old Republic bounty charters and Sith Empire mercenary rolls show how bounty hunter contractors were hired to bypass political treaties. Mandalorian foundling laws and Hutt kajidic codes both influenced how hunters like Mercurial Swift negotiate payment and honor.

In the modern era, Mercurial Swift competed on postings issued by the Empire, the Rebellion, the Hutt Cartel, and independent monarchs alike. Swift competed alongside Boba Fett, Valance, and Nakano Lash during carbonite theft crisis—Core agility against Rim brutality in marquee comics event. Post-Endor guild restructuring and New Republic amnesty debates still reference contracts linked to Mercurial Swift. Mandalorian-era postings on Nevarro and Mos Espa show bounty hunter specialists remain essential to galactic order—and chaos.

Mercurial Swift operated in war zones where capture alive paid more than kill, and both paid more than failure. Swift pursued Solo carbonite puck across Nar Shaddaa and Core worlds, clashed with rival hunters, and navigated post-Endor guild lawlessness. KOTOR-era Nar Shaddaa boards and TOR-era Great Galactic War contracts show earlier generations of bounty hunter hunters in the same blood-stained market. Jedi, Sith, and clone troopers alike learned to respect or fear Mercurial Swift's approach to pursuit and extraction.
